title: Operator bootstrap & scale heuristics — private control plane (draft)
body:
Purpose:
This is a working runbook for operator handoff during initial bootstrap and routine scaling/rotation operations for Private Control Plane (VPC / on-prem). Focus is on reproducible TF workflows, safe node rotations, KV cache warm-up strategies, and pragmatic heuristics for scaling decisions in mixed latency/cost SLOs.

Audience:
Operators, SREs, platform engineers responsible for commissioning private control planes and triaging scale/upgrade events.

Status and intent:
- Draft: operationally testable but not yet approved for customer-facing SOPs.
- Contains explicit commands and TF notes to make day-one onboarding less ad-hoc.

Quick overview checklist (day-zero):
- Confirm VPC network peering, route tables, and egress NAT for controlplane nodes.
- Verify KMS/HSM credentials and access policy for controlplane service accounts.
- Ensure monitoring (Prometheus exporters, node-level) and tracing endpoints are reachable.
- Create a TF state backend snapshot (s3/gcs) and lock before any changes.
- Run `terraform plan -var-file=customer.tfvars` and capture plan as artifact.

Pre-boot considerations (network & security):
- MTU mismatches often surface on baremetal NICs (1500 vs jumbo). If customers use jumbo frames ensure all hops accept configured MTU.
- Firewall rules: open 6443 (API), 2379-2380 (etcd) internal-only; controlplane nodes should not expose etcd to Internet.
- DNS: confirm internal DNS zones are resolvable and clients can reach controlplane FQDNs.

Terraform module pragmatics (notes from field runs):
- Make modules idempotent: avoid implicit ordering that requires manual tainting. Prefer explicit depends_on for bootstrap resources that must exist before controlplane starts (e.g., kms_key -> secrets -> controlplane).
- Use lifecycle.ignore_changes for fields managed by the controlplane runtime (e.g., instance metadata that runtime updates). Document each ignore with a comment.
- For node pools, model them as separate module instances per class (api, etcd, worker). This reduces blast radius when scaling/rotating.
- State drift: for onprem environments where operators manually change host configs, add a small reconciliation job that detects drift and produces a PR to terraform modules rather than letting drift accumulate.
- Secrets: avoid storing large cert blobs in TF state; store certs in KMS-backed secrets manager and reference by ID.

Idempotency gotchas and recovery steps:
- If a `terraform apply` errors halfway with some resources created, do not immediately re-run apply. First: `terraform refresh` to reconcile state, then `terraform plan` to see what would change.
- If a resource must be replaced but provider refuses (e.g., onprem IP allocation), use `terraform state rm <resource>` to orphan, then recreate using a controlled apply with explicit `-target` to avoid unexpected deletes.

Scaling heuristics (when to add capacity):
- Primary signals: CPU% sustained > 70% for 10m across controlplane component metrics, request queue depth > threshold, and token generation latency P95 trending up > 20%.
- Secondary checks: KV cache hit ratio, worker GPU memory pressure, and infra-level throttles (pod evictions).
- Scale up sequence: 1) warm nodes (launch nodes but keep out of rotation), 2) ensure runtime warms KV cache (see warm-up step), 3) add to rotation and ramp load over 5–15 minutes.

Warm-up and cache handling:
- To avoid cold-KV penalties, expose an internal warmup endpoint that replays small representative prefixes into new nodes. The warmup should be conservative (1–2k tokens/session) and driven from a controlplane job.
- Warmup policy: keep at least one node warmed in each availability zone/host-pool before promoting a node to serving.

Node rotation pattern (safe rolling procedure):
- Use cordon/drain semantics at orchestrator level. If baremetal without orchestration, add a health-check bypass in the load-balancer before shutting down.
- Drain sequence: 1) mark node Unavailable in service registry, 2) wait for in-flight requests to drain (configurable grace, default 60s), 3) wait for KV cache persist/snapshot if required, 4) remove from LB and shut down.
- Reprovision sequence: reimage -> apply user-data -> run post-boot checks (connectivity, certs) -> run warmup -> add back to registry.

Upgrade plan (minor and major):
- Minor (<patch/minor): can usually be done with rolling restarts of runtime containers. Test on a single non-primary node first.
- Major (breaking changes or etcd schema): require a blue/green deploy when possible. Blue/green approach: deploy parallel controlplane in separate node pool and gradually switch clients by updating routing policy. If parallel pool not possible, do canary rolling upgrades with aggressive monitoring and automated rollback triggers.
- Automated rollback triggers: P95 latency > 2x baseline for >5m, error rate >2% absolute increase, or reconciliation failures in core controlplane components.

Operator handoff checklist (transfer to customer's platform team):
- Provide terraform module versions and pin file.
- Provide runbook: exact CLI commands to scale/drain/rotate and emergency rollback steps.
- Share monitoring dashboards and alert runbooks with on-call rotations.
- Provide access matrix for KMS keys, TF state backend, and controlplane admin credentials.

Common failure modes and remediation quick notes:
- Failed etcd quorum after node upgrade: immediately isolate nodes upgraded during the window and attempt to restore previous cluster membership. If quorum cannot be recovered, restore etcd from a recent snapshot following documented snapshot restore flow.
- Node boots but fails health checks due to time skew: check NTP and host clock; time skew >5s can cause TLS issues with cert validation.
- TF apply reports cyclic dependency: break cycle by introducing temporary `null_resource` with depends_on to sequence bootstrapping. Clean up null_resource after stable deployment.

Sample useful commands (reference):
- TF lock & snapshot: `terraform state pull > state-$(date +%F-%s).json`
- Plan with varfile: `terraform plan -var-file=customer.tfvars -out=plan.tfplan`
- Apply targeted: `terraform apply -target=module.controlplane_node_pool.api plan.tfplan`
- Drain (k8s): `kubectl cordon NODE && kubectl drain NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=60`
- Warmup curl example: `curl -sS -X POST https://internal-warmup.local/prime -d '{"prefixes":["The patient", "Generate code for"]}'`

Post-op validation (after any scale/rotation/update):
- Confirm all nodes report Healthy in service registry and LB.
- Confirm KV cache hit ratio within expected band.
- Confirm P95 latency and error rate are at or below pre-op baseline.
- Confirm no new reconciliation errors in controlplane logs for 30m.

Open TODOs and follow-ups:
- Add automated warmup job into Terraform modules so new pools can be pre-warmed via TF-driven lifecycle hooks.
- Capture warmup metrics and add synthetic transactions to onboarding checklist.
- Create a small helper CLI that wraps the common TF + cordon/drain patterns to reduce operator error.

Notes from recent field test (2025-10-27):
- Manual warmup reduced P99 tail by ~18% on a 10-node scale event.
- Observed TF state drift in edge site where operators updated hostnames manually; added reconciliation job to mitigate.

Appendix: quick TF snippet patterns (operator notes):
- Separate node pool example (pseudo):
  module "controlplane_api_pool" {
    source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//node-pool"
    node_class = "api"
    desired_count = var.api_desired_count
  }

- lifecycle ignore sample:
  resource "aws_instance" "cp_node" {
    # ...
    lifecycle {
      ignore_changes = [metadata] # updated by controlplane agent
    }
  }

If anything here is unclear or you hit an unexpected state during a run, slack #private-cp-ops and ping an on-call. Keep a step-by-step transcript and attach the terraform plan and state snapshot for postmortem.

End of draft runbook.
